Subject: KMS & customer-managed keys — follow-up from discovery

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking time to meet today. Quick recap of the security/compliance items we covered and suggested next steps.

Summary from today's discovery call:
- SOC 2: You asked whether Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report — yes, we have a SOC 2 Type II (2025) attestation. I've attached a 1-page summary for your initial review.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support data processing controls needed for GDPR; for HIPAA, we can support a covered entity customer's workflows (BAA discussions to follow if needed).
- Encryption: All customer data is encrypted in-transit (TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS where requested) and at-rest using envelope encryption.
- Key management options discussed:
  - Standard: Redwood-managed keys (we manage CMKs and wrap keys).
  - Customer-managed keys (CMK/BYOK): We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (e.g., AWS KMS) and can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping/unwrapping operations.
  - HSM-backed keys: For customers requiring FIPS 140-2/140-3 HSM-backed keys, we support integrations that allow the customer's HSM/KMS to be the root of trust (CloudHSM, external HSM vendors) — we do not persist unencrypted plaintext keys in our control plane.

Attachments: redwood-kms-overview.pdf (tech brief), redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf (one-page).

Action items / proposed next steps:
1) Could you confirm whether FinBank requires HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3) or if a cloud-KMS BYOK model is acceptable?
2) Please complete and return the vendor security questionnaire (you mentioned you could share it) — we can populate answers and return within 2 business days.
3) If helpful, let's schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45 min) next week (wk of Jul 6) with Dev (cc'd) to walk key rotation, audit logs, and network/data residency details.

If there are any other compliance artifacts you need (encryption architecture diagram, KMS flow, or SOC 2 report copy), let me know and I'll get them to you.

Best,

Quick answers/asks for now:
- SOC 2: Please share the full SOC 2 Type II report (or a redacted copy) and any complementary security docs. The 1-page summary is helpful but we'll need the report for procurement.
- KMS/Keys: FinBank strongly prefers HSM-backed keys for any customer-managed keys used for production encryption. We are looking for FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or FIPS 140-3 assurances where keys are generated or protected. Please confirm whether Redwood can operate with the customer's HSM or CloudHSM-backed KMS so that the root key never leaves our control.
- BYOK: We prefer a BYOK model where FinBank controls the CMK and can rotate/delete keys on demand. Does Redwood support key rotation initiated by the customer and immediate revocation/soft-delete?
- Audit logs: We need detailed key-usage logs (key unwrap/wrap calls, timestamps, principal) retained for at least 12 months and accessible for audit/export.
- Data residency: Confirm whether any key material or wraps would transit outside the US region during normal operations or failover.

Attached: FinBank-vendor-questionnaire.xlsx (please return with answers).

Hi Alice — really appreciate the detail. We're happy to proceed on all three asks (SOC2 report, questionnaire, technical deep-dive). Please find a couple items attached: a link to our full SOC 2 access request (we can provide a redacted PDF under an NDA) and a draft responses document that our team will use to fill the questionnaire.

Short answers to the key points you raised:
- HSM-backed keys: We support integrations where the customer's KMS/HSM is the root of trust (e.g., AWS CloudHSM or on-prem HSM with a supported gateway). In that model, the root keys are generated and protected by your HSM and Redwood performs envelope encryption using wrapped DEKs.
- BYOK & rotation: Customer-initiated key rotation is supported; keys can be rotated and revoked according to your KMS policies. We do not persist plaintext CMKs in our control plane.
- Audit logs: We emit detailed KMS audit events (wrap/unwrap requests, timestamps, service principals) and can surface those through our Console and through streaming to your logging endpoint (S3/CloudWatch/Logstash). Retention and export can be configured to meet the 12-month retention requirement.
- Data residency: By default, key unwrap/wrap operations occur in the region where the customer's KMS is located when configured as customer-managed; we can ensure key operations do not cross region boundaries in normal operations.

Next steps I propose:
1) I've attached a draft response (internal) to the questionnaire — Dev and Aditya are already reviewing.
2) Dev to run the technical deep-dive with your infra/security team on Wed Jul 7 11:00 AM EDT (please confirm).
3) We will prepare a redacted SOC 2 Type II PDF for your procurement under NDA and upload to the Drive link.

Marissa / Aditya — sharing quick technical points we should include in the questionnaire draft before sending to FinBank. These are internal notes (do not forward to the customer until we sync):

- KMS integrations: We support envelope encryption. CEKs/DEKs are generated per-tenant and wrapped using the customer's CMK (via AWS KMS GenerateDataKey with CMK ARN) when configured for BYOK. The wrapped key material is stored in our metadata store; plaintext DEKs are only in memory during encryption ops.
- HSM support: For customers requiring FIPS 140-2/3, we can integrate with CloudHSM or external HSMs. The CMK can be provisioned in the customer's HSM; Redwood never holds the HSM root key.
- Key rotation & revocation: Rotation is driven by the customer's KMS policy. If a CMK is revoked/deleted, we can re-encrypt data with a new DEK using a new CMK, or follow your preferred migration pattern. Immediately revoking a CMK will prevent future unwraps in Redwood (affects read operations).
- Audit logs: We log wrap/unwrap (API principal, timestamp, operation_id) and can export to the customer's logging destination. Default retention is 12 months; we can extend if required under an enterprise add-on.
- Data residency: When configured with customer-managed KMS, wrap/unwrap calls are executed in the customer-specified region; cross-region failover will only occur if explicitly enabled and agreed in the SLA.
- SOC2 access: Recommend we provide a redacted SOC2 Type II PDF under NDA and schedule procurement review.

I'll be available for the technical call on Wed Jul 7 11:00 AM EDT. I'll prepare a short diagram showing key flow (DEK generation, wrapping, storage) and include a sample sequence (API calls).
